name: FirstCash Holdings, Inc.
moat_justification: Largest international pawn operator (3,300+ stores across the U.S., Latin America and the U.K.) with scale in collateral appraisal and liquidation, state/local licensing barriers and a proven acquisition platform (H&T closed 2025, Ramsdens pending). Gross margin has held 46-56% for a decade and rose 47.8% -> 50.3% FY23-25; ROE rose 11.0% -> 14.5% over the same years (fundamentals.json; roic_proxy is null because the filer does not tag operating income). That is a moderate, scale-based moat, not a wide one: customers are transactional with no switching costs, local competition is fragmented but real, and returns are capped by pawn-rate regulation, FX and the declining AFF point-of-sale segment.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.5x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.7%) vs bull-case tier B (15.4%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Quality pawn franchise, moat 5/10 — TTM owner's earnings $13.50/share but the weighted IRR is 13.0% at $214.78, short of the 15% hurdle; it clears 15% at or below the $177.10 weighted IV@15%.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Scale: largest international pawn operator, 3,300+ stores in the U.S., Latin America and U.K.
Collateral appraisal and liquidation expertise built over decades, hard to replicate store-by-store
Licensing and regulatory compliance barriers in pawn lending across many jurisdictions
Acquisition platform in a fragmented industry (H&T 2025, Ramsdens pending) with geographic diversification
Counter-cyclical pawn demand and durable gross margins (47.8% FY23 to 50.3% FY25)
moat_against: No network effects or switching costs — pawn customers are transactional and price-sensitive
Fragmented local competition from independent pawnshops, online lenders and lease-to-own providers
Regulatory risk: pawn-rate caps and consumer-credit rules (incl. the AFF point-of-sale business)
FX exposure (Mexican peso and now sterling) and gold-price exposure via jewelry collateral
AFF retail point-of-sale segment shrinking (management guides its net revenue down 20-25% in 2026) and goodwill-heavy balance sheet from acquisitions

overrides.source: Average of the last three filed fiscal years' capex from financials_history.csv (FY2023 $60,148,000; FY2024 $68,245,000; FY2025 $54,906,000; PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets, 10-K filed 2026-02-09)
